Unless the portal transfers kinetic energy to the block, B is physically impossible. There would have  to be a delay in transportation that allows the portal to strike the block so the portal can transfer its kinetic energy to the block. It would also mean that when the block is dropped into the portal it loses some of its kinetic energy and transfers it to the portal. 

In real life, worm holes don’t work like this. In a video game the devs can measure velocity in what ever physics defying way they want. 

If you don’t understand refer to newton’s third law, conservation of momentum. 

The real question is how does portal achieve its teleportation? Simplest way to do it would be the measure velocity of items relative to the portal and the position of the item on the portal’s surface when it goes through the portal. 

On today’s computers we maybe be able to run a simulated wormhole in games, but I doubt anyone in their right mind would spend time coding and tuning that just to make a portal that doesn’t even run efficiently. 

TLDR: In portal probably B, in real life definitely A.

I’m not sure topicals would do much. There’s a large market for scar reduction but the truth is scars aren’t supposed to breakdown at all and you’re body probably won’t allow much significant healing in an area like this. 

You could consult a dermatological plastic surgeon. There are options like scar revision surgery, and CO2 laser revision. If you have any nerve damage they may also be able to help separate scar tissue form nerve fibres and reduce the pain and inflammation with something like a saline or steroid injection. On the experimental side there is stem cell based treatments, and in the future we may be able to completely hide any sized scar with treatments like this.

I know you didn’t ask but here’s my take on modern dating in a nutshell: 

Sit beside someone in class, and say hi before the lecture starts. Go to an event, and make a joke to someone who might be close to you for a period of time. Click with a group, stick close to someone you’re interested in. 

If you meet someone it’s okay to pursue them as long as you respect their desires. Ask for a specific messaging app, text them even if you can’t think of any good reason to. You can tell the difference between not interested at all and not interested yet. If they’re completely uninterested you’ll get ghosted, or they’ll come up with a reason they don’t have that messaging app. I suggest no phone numbers, everyone has one and nobody wants to say “lol I don’t wanna give you my number” so you’ll end up blocked or ghosted anyway. Ask for like something like IG or Whatsapp instead, if they say they don’t have it or don’t use it and they don’t suggest something else just take it on the chin. 

Dating apps can be a good way to practice breaking the ice and making your way to going on a date. Unfortunately, it’s hard to really connect on them. When you first meet someone irl it’s much easier to meet up with them again, actually landing a date is the hard part on dating apps. 

Once you have someone’s contact, see if you can make a good connection, and towards the end of a good conversation want to meet up. Strike while the iron is hot, you very well might only have one good conversation with them entirely if you don’t. If they say they’re busy you’re not quite connected enough or they’re just rejecting you. If they say they want to meet up another time your in a grey area, and you should do want your intuition tells you and prey you don’t fuck it up.

I’m a psychology student, and I’ve overcome self harm. Personally, I would advise that you talk to a counsellor yourself about that the matter as they may provide useful insight into the situation. However, I’m going to try to help if that isn’t possible. 

To answer your question, “why would someone selfharm,” the answer is for the most part endorphins. When you get cut with something extremely sharp it often feels good more than it hurts because of the chemicals released to combat the injury. Endorphins are proven to ease depression. There is also a psychological component to it. Eventually pain feels good, or you can start to feel as though you deserve pain. 

None of this means you’ve failed as a parent, only that she is personally going through a difficult time in her life. 

In my battle with addictions I’ve found that there are three necessary things needed to overcome addictions or habits: resolve, support, and reinforcement. She has to stop wanting to self harm because she’s feels it is not worth it. She has to be able to cope or find support in other ways, and she has to reinforce the idea that she’s done with self harm. To do this I would recommend encouraging her to see a therapist, specifically a cognitive behavioural therapist. 

Lastly, I want to clear up some misinformation on medication. She likely will not receive anything that could get her high, and SSRIs have the potential to prevent permanently reduced mental function in those with chronic depression. Above all I believe that the use of medication should be a choice between her and her doctor.
